open_points.subject: OwnerFormField target mapping
open_points.text: its name, whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives, and how its text is read
open_points.question: How does a row identify the exact request or values field that receives the parsed value, including a nested field or tuple position?
options: The form name must equal a flat model-field name
A separate owner-interface mapping supplies the target path
OwnerFormField must retain an explicit target path and tuple-position marks
open_points.default_guess: Restore an explicit target path, including tuple-position marks.

witness.initial: An owner form field must populate a nested or positional value.
events: The owner submits the named field.
The owner interface looks up its OwnerFormField row and parses the text.
outcomes: The interface treats the name as a flat model-field name and cannot address the nested or positional value.
The interface applies an unstated path convention and writes the nested or positional value.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees either a rejected submission or a value written to a different place.

open_points.subject: OWNER_FORM_FIELDS page and action scope
open_points.text: A row of the owner form table: one field of the owner's pages
open_points.question: What identifies the owner page or action to which each row applies?
options: Every row applies to every owner page
Field names are globally unique and implicitly identify their page or action
Each row must carry an owner action, route, or page identifier
A separate table maps actions or pages to form-field rows
open_points.default_guess: Associate every row explicitly with an OwnerAction.

witness.initial: Two owner pages exist and accept different sets of fields.
events: The owner submits one of the pages.
The owner interface consults the single OWNER_FORM_FIELDS table.
outcomes: It accepts every globally listed field on that page.
It filters rows using an unstated page-to-field association.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees different fields accepted or refused.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField name uniqueness
open_points.question: May two rows share a field name, and if so, what key unambiguously selects a row when submitted text is read?
options: Names are globally unique across all owner pages
The key is the pair of name and OwnerFormCarrier
Names may repeat by page or action, which must also be part of the key
open_points.default_guess: Require uniqueness of the tuple (owner action, carrier, field name).

witness.initial: Two owner pages use the same HTML field name with different value kinds or carriers.
events: The data provider contains both rows.
The owner submits that field name on one page.
The owner interface selects a row.
outcomes: The implementation rejects the release because names must be globally unique.
The implementation permits both rows and resolves them using page or carrier context.
witness.observer: The owner, whose submitted text is either rejected or parsed under one of two rules.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField closed-list parsing
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: Where does a row identify the particular closed list and the member-value mapping used to parse its text?
options: Infer the list from the destination model field's type
Add the enumeration or closed-list identity to OwnerFormField
Use one global closed list for all such rows
Define the mapping separately in the owner interface
open_points.default_guess: Identify the destination field explicitly and infer its enumeration from that field's declared type.

witness.initial: Two owner fields are read as members of different closed lists, and both lists contain different members for the same submitted text.
events: The owner interface reads a row whose value kind only says that it is a closed-list value.
outcomes: The interface resolves the text against the destination field's enumeration.
The interface resolves it against another unstated or global list.
witness.observer: The owner and downstream service, which receive different enumeration values or a refusal.

open_points.subject: FormValueKind conversion semantics
open_points.text: as text, as a whole number, as yes or no, or as one of a closed list
open_points.question: What exact lexical forms, normalization, and failure rules define whole-number, yes-or-no, and closed-list parsing?
options: Use the host language's default conversions
Accept only a specified canonical wire spelling for each kind
Let each owner page choose its accepted spellings
open_points.default_guess: Specify canonical, locale-independent spellings and reject every non-canonical value.

witness.initial: An owner submits a yes-or-no field with text such as "on" or a whole number with surrounding whitespace.
events: The owner interface parses the submitted text according to FormValueKind.
outcomes: The implementation accepts and normalizes the text using permissive host-language or HTML conventions.
The implementation accepts only literal canonical spellings and refuses it.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees acceptance in one implementation and refusal in another.

open_points.subject: query-field coverage
open_points.text: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form
open_points.question: Does OWNER_FORM_FIELDS still describe owner query fields, or are query parameters excluded and specified elsewhere?
options: Query fields are excluded from OWNER_FORM_FIELDS
Query fields are treated as form fields
OwnerFormField must explicitly distinguish form fields from query fields
open_points.default_guess: Explicitly include the transport or location of each field and retain query-field coverage.

witness.initial: An owner action receives a user-selected value through its query string.
events: The owner invokes the action with the query value.
The owner interface decides whether OWNER_FORM_FIELDS governs that value.
outcomes: The interface validates and parses the query value through the table.
The interface ignores the table and applies an independently chosen query-decoding rule.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees different acceptance or interpretation of the same URL.

open_points.subject: OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK
open_points.question: After tuple positions were removed from OwnerFormField's facts, what does this exported constant mean, who uses it, and should it remain in the data closure?
options: Remove the constant and all positional-field support
Keep it as syntax interpreted by the owner interface despite its absence from OwnerFormField
Restore positional target information to OwnerFormField
open_points.default_guess: Restore positional target information to OwnerFormField if positional fields remain supported; otherwise remove the constant.

witness.initial: A release contains OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK while the OwnerFormField model has no positional fact.
events: A generated consumer imports the constant.
outcomes: The consumer treats the constant as obsolete and never recognizes positional names.
The consumer invents a convention in which the constant encodes tuple positions in field names.
witness.observer: The owner, whose positional form value is either decoded or ignored/refused.
